Sprint 2: - _After the design is evaluated and planned, this is the main story ticket Lean Data Weighting & Round Robin pools for implementation._  

As an admin I would like to have a centralized scalable architecture in Salesforce to allow and manage the current and future assignment of mgos by weighted allocation across the business for any field sales territory that is considered an ALRA territory. The following needs to hold true:

‌

* In territories where the pipeline reps are working (LA & NY) they are to get the same portion of MGOs as an LRA). - _pending confirmation of %_ 
* ALRAs will get an inverted weighting where the majority of the MGOs will be weighted to be assigned to the ALRAs in the markets where it operates. 
* In an ALRA market, non ALRA reps will have an equal round robin assignment amongst themselves. Those reps will have weighting at a lower level than than the ALRA.  

‌

**Notes:**

* MGO LCO leads created from the funnel are included. 
* Lead escalation will be implemented for HV escalation for the BDRs **after** the BDR has qualified the lead during the lead qualification process.  [Sales-9129](https://trr-prod.atlassian.net/browse/SALES-9129)
* 

---

* The following is business as usual - _current process_ with no change:

    * BDR pools.
    * SGOs 
    * BDRs will evaluate if a lead should stay as an LCO lead after their qualification and will adjust the lead method to match what should be the proper sales method. 
    * The ship direct flow auto converts leads into an opportunities, bypassing the BDRs (if the consignor finishes the funnel). This process and these leads will not be included in the scope.
    * Consignment kits also follow this process of being auto-converted and assigned - these are also outside of the scope.
    * Opportunities for Repeat Consignors

fields.description:
‌

**Objective:** Understand what Agentforce co-worker is, how it works within Salesforce, and how it could be useful for our teams and business workflows.

### Background

Salesforce Agentforce introduces AI-powered agents and co-workers that can support users by answering questions, assisting with tasks, automating workflows, and surfacing relevant information from Salesforce data and connected systems. This spike will evaluate the capabilities, architecture, setup requirements, and potential use cases for adopting Agentforce co-worker in our Salesforce environment.

### Goals

* Research what Agentforce co-worker is and how it differs from traditional Salesforce automation, bots, and AI assistants.
* Understand how Agentforce co-worker works, including required Salesforce features, data access, permissions, prompts, actions, topics, and integration points.
* Identify practical use cases where Agentforce co-worker could help our users within Salesforce.
* Assess benefits, limitations, risks, licensing considerations, security implications, and implementation effort.
* Recommend whether further proof-of-concept or implementation work should be created.

### Scope

* Review Salesforce documentation and available Agentforce co-worker product materials.
* Evaluate configuration options and high-level architecture.
* Identify candidate use cases for our Salesforce org.
* Document findings, risks, dependencies, and recommendations.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Document a clear explanation of what Agentforce co-worker is.
- [ ] Describe how Agentforce co-worker works within Salesforce, including key components and dependencies.
- [ ] List at least three potential use cases relevant to our Salesforce users or business processes.
- [ ] Identify benefits, limitations, risks, security considerations, and licensing or enablement requirements.
- [ ] Provide a recommendation for next steps, such as no action, deeper evaluation, or proof of concept.

### Deliverables

* Spike findings document or Confluence summary.
* Use case shortlist with expected value and complexity.
* Recommendation for next steps and estimated follow-up work.

fields.description:
## User story

**As a** Salesforce platform owner,
**I want** a data-driven estimate of additional storage capacity required to enable **Einstein Activity Capture (EAC)** and **Salesforce Inbox** for planned user cohorts,
**So that** we can procure storage and define retention/archival policies **before** rollout — avoiding production storage limits and unplanned overage costs.

---

## Context

TRR production org storage was previously reported at **\~97% utilized** ([SALES-2654](https://trr-prod.atlassian.net/browse/SALES-2654)). EAC and Inbox are prerequisites for the Outreach program ([SALES-8753](https://trr-prod.atlassian.net/browse/SALES-8753)) — unified activity timeline (Req 1.4), Phase 4 Maps routing via EAC calendar sync, and rep productivity via Inbox + Gmail integration ([SALES-8918](https://trr-prod.atlassian.net/browse/SALES-8918)).

**Why this matters now (Summer '26+ platform changes):**

| Capability | Default storage behavior | Native SF storage impact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **EAC — email capture** | Historically stored on Salesforce-managed external storage (AWS) | **Optional:** "Sync Email as Salesforce Activity" writes `EmailMessage` + `Task` records — **counts against org data storage** (irreversible once enabled) |
| **EAC — calendar/events** | Synced as native `Event` records | **Yes** — consumes data storage |
| **EAC — contacts** | Synced as native `Contact` records (where matched) | **Yes** — consumes data storage |
| **Salesforce Inbox** | Email/calendar activity stored as native records | **Yes** — full reporting/automation; higher native storage footprint than legacy EAC-only capture |

**Key configuration decisions that change sizing:**

* Full email body vs. **header-only** capture
* User cohort size (pilot vs. full sales org)
* Sync scope (all email vs. matched-to-CRM only)
* Whether to enable **Sync Email as Salesforce Activity** (required for Flow/reporting on email content; permanent decision)
* Historical backfill window (Salesforce caps at **180 days** for migrated/backfilled email data)
* Retention/archival strategy (`Work with Archived Activities`, deletion policies)

---

## Scope

### In scope

* Quantify **incremental storage** (GB + record counts) for planned EAC + Inbox rollout scenarios
* Model **12- and 24-month** growth projections by user cohort
* Recommend **minimum additional storage to procure** (with buffer) and timing
* Document **configuration recommendations** that minimize storage while meeting product requirements
* Assess interaction with ongoing storage optimization ([SALES-9334](https://trr-prod.atlassian.net/browse/SALES-9334) COI/Comp Calculations spike)

---

## Investigation tasks

### 1. Baseline current storage

* \[ \] Current org utilization: data storage, file storage, % used (PROD + representative sandbox)
* \[ \] Headroom before hard limits / performance degradation
* \[ \] Top consuming objects today (Setup → Storage Usage)
* \[ \] Existing activity volume: `Task`, `Event`, `EmailMessage` counts and growth trend (if Enhanced Email already enabled)

### 2. Define rollout scenarios

Document at least **3 scenarios** (example — adjust with Product):

| Scenario | Users | EAC config | Inbox | Email sync mode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A — Pilot** | TBD (e.g., Concierge MVP) | Calendar + matched email | Pilot cohort | Header-only |
| **B — Standard** | TBD (inside + field sales) | Full EAC | Enabled | Header-only |
| **C — Full native** | TBD (max cohort) | Full EAC + Sync Email as Activity | Enabled | Full body |

For each scenario capture:

* Licensed user count
* Avg emails/day/user, meetings/day/user (from Google Workspace audit or sample cohort)
* Match rate to CRM records (Lead/Contact/Opportunity/Account)
* Internal vs. external email ratio (excluded emails don't sync)

### 3. Size incremental storage

Estimate net-new records and storage for:

* `EmailMessage` + related `Task` records
* `Event` (calendar sync for Maps / outreach timeline)
* Incremental `Contact` updates/creates from EAC matching
* Attachments/inline images (if applicable under chosen config)

**Sizing formula (document assumptions):**

```
Annual email records ≈ users × emails/day × 250 working days × match_rate
Annual event records ≈ users × meetings/day × 250 × sync_rate
Storage (GB) ≈ (record_count × avg_record_size_KB) / 1,048,576
```

Include **low / expected / high** ranges.

### 4. Configuration & retention recommendations

* \[ \] Recommend email capture mode (header-only vs. full body) per scenario
* \[ \] Assess whether **Sync Email as Salesforce Activity** is required for Outreach Phase 2–4 (Flow, Agentforce, reporting) — if yes, quantify delta vs. legacy external storage
* \[ \] Evaluate archival options: Salesforce activity archive, retention windows (EAC external retention 6–24 months vs. native record lifecycle)
* \[ \] Identify storage freed by concurrent cleanup initiatives (COI/Comp Calc, analytics cleanup) to compute **net** capacity need

### 5. Procurement & rollout gate

* \[ \] Recommended **additional storage SKU/blocks** to purchase (with 20–30% buffer)
* \[ \] Go/no-go criteria: minimum free capacity % before expanding EAC/Inbox beyond pilot
* \[ \] Monitoring plan post-enablement (monthly storage burn rate dashboard)

---

## Deliverables

1. **Storage sizing workbook** — assumptions, scenarios, 12/24-month projections (GB + record counts)
2. **Configuration decision memo** — recommended EAC/Inbox settings with storage vs. functionality trade-offs
3. **Procurement recommendation** — additional capacity required, target purchase date, estimated cost (if available from SF account team)

---

---

## Dependencies

| Dependency | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| [SALES-8753](https://trr-prod.atlassian.net/browse/SALES-8753) Outreach Automation Foundation | Parent epic — defines user cohorts and timeline |
| [SALES-8918](https://trr-prod.atlassian.net/browse/SALES-8918) Turn on Inbox | Completed spike — informs Inbox scope |
| [SALES-9095](https://trr-prod.atlassian.net/browse/SALES-9095) EAC health check | Workspace audit data feeds volume assumptions |
| [SALES-2654](https://trr-prod.atlassian.net/browse/SALES-2654) | Prior org-wide storage analysis |
| [SALES-9334](https://trr-prod.atlassian.net/browse/SALES-9334) | Parallel storage optimization — net capacity calculation |
| Product / Sales Ops | Confirm rollout cohorts and pilot timeline |
| Google Workspace admin | Email/calendar volume samples |

---

fields.description:
## User story

**As a** Salesforce administrator,
**I want** to assess, test, and enable the **Enable Profile Filtering** release update before enforcement,
**So that** users who legitimately need cross-profile visibility retain access via **View All Profiles**, while all other users are restricted from browsing org profile metadata — improving security without breaking admin, ops, or reporting workflows.

---

## Release update details

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Release update** | Enable Profile Filtering |
| **Category** | Security |
| **Available from** | Summer '26 |
| **Complete steps by** | **September 1, 2026** |
| **Enforcement** | **Winter '27** (auto-enabled if not completed) |
| **Current status** | 0% — 0 of 3 steps complete |
| **Test run** | Supported (sandbox or production) |
| **Setup path** | Setup → Release Updates → _Enable Profile Filtering_ |

### What is changing

Profile filtering **limits users from viewing any profile names other than their own** unless they are assigned the **View All Profiles** permission.

To improve org security, Salesforce is **enabling Profile Filtering by default**. After enforcement, users without **View All Profiles** will not see other profile names in lookups, user detail pages, reports, or related UI.

‌

### Created Permission Set

* View_All_Profiles

### Updated Permission Sets and Permission Set Groups

* TRR_SUMO_CEP_Admin_Users
* TRR_SUMO_CEP_Manager_Users
* TRR_SUMO_CEP_Standard_Users
* TRR_SUMO_Pilot_Admin_User
* TRR_SUMO_Pilot_Standard_User
* Owner_Change_Approval
* Sales_Compensation_Comp_Admin
* Sales_Compensation_Sales_Admin

---

## Risk assessment

| Risk tier | **High** — Security enforcement with broad user-facing impact |
| --- | --- |
| **Likely impact areas** | User record profile lookups; user management screens; reports/dashboards filtered by Profile; Sales Ops admin workflows; delegated admin tasks; custom Apex/LWC referencing Profile names; integrations querying Profile metadata |
| **Mitigation** | Audit users needing cross-profile visibility → assign **View All Profiles** via permission set (least privilege); test in sandbox before production enablement |

---

## Work plan (3 Release Update steps)

### Step 1 — Review & assess impact

* \[ \] Open **Setup → Release Updates → Enable Profile Filtering** and review Salesforce guidance
* \[ \] Document current vs. new behavior in Release Updates tracker
* \[ \] Inventory users/roles that **require** visibility into profiles beyond their own (admins, Sales Ops, support, security)
* \[ \] Review TRR profiles, permission sets, and PSGs for existing **View All Profiles** grants
* \[ \] Scan codebase and integrations for Profile name dependencies
* \[ \] Identify reports/dashboards using Profile as a filter or column

### Step 2 — Test run (sandbox)

* \[ \] Enable **Test Run** in preview sandbox
* \[ \] Validate standard users can no longer browse other profile names
* \[ \] Validate privileged users with **View All Profiles** PS retain required access
* \[ \] Regression test: user creation, profile assignment, Sales Ops provisioning
* \[ \] Document failures and required permission set assignments

### Step 3 — Remediate & enable in production

* \[ \] Create or update permission set granting **View All Profiles** for approved users only
* \[ \] Assign permission set in sandbox → validate → deploy to production
* \[ \] Enable release update in **production** before **Sep 1, 2026** deadline
* \[ \] Mark all 3 steps complete in Setup → Release Updates
* \[ \] Communicate change to affected teams

---

## Acceptance criteria

* \[ \] Release update impact assessed and documented
* \[ \] Sandbox **Test Run** completed with no unresolved blockers
* \[ \] **View All Profiles** permission set created and assigned (least-privilege documented)
* \[ \] Release update **enabled in production** with 3/3 steps complete
* \[ \] Completed **before September 1, 2026**

---

## Dependencies

* [SALES-9331](https://trr-prod.atlassian.net/browse/SALES-9331) — Profiles/PS/PSG cleanup
* [SALES-9332](https://trr-prod.atlassian.net/browse/SALES-9332) — Profile discovery spike

fields.description:
**Summary:** Pre-booked in-home appointments that meet High-Value criteria keep their original rep — appointment time remains BDR-adjustable — with reporting to identify affected consignors and a consumable process doc for L&D/BDRs

**Description:**  
 As a sales leader, I want pre-booked in-home appointments that turn out to meet High-Value criteria to stay with the originally assigned rep, so that we don't disrupt the client relationship with a rep swap — while still allowing normal appointment-time changes, being able to report on which consignors this happened to, and giving L&D/BDRs a clear reference for how this scenario works.

**Scope:**

* **This is a scope change to the existing SUMO in-home appointment ticket (Sales-9192)** — not a net-new story. This is the confirmed RevOps decision, resolving the open design question from the project plan (cancel/rebook vs. retain) in favor of retain-the-rep.
* **Applies to new MGOs only** — not to existing/legacy leads or appointments booked prior to this scope change. **This is part of the broader ALRA rollout and is inclusive of the High-Value escalation functionality feature** — this scope change is part of that feature, not a separate mechanism. **Go-live for this is August 3rd**, aligned to the overall ALRA rollout date.
* **Applies to ALRA territories only** — territories not live in the ALRA model are out of scope for this behavior.
* If a pre-booked in-home appointment is later identified as meeting High-Value criteria, the rep/host originally assigned is **not changed** — no reassignment to a different (e.g., higher-tier) rep occurs.
* **If a client was assigned a rep through booking on the CLP, that rep is retained** when the client is subsequently re-booked into an in-home service — no reassignment to a new rep occurs as part of that transition.
* The BDR retains normal ability to change/reschedule the **appointment time** — this restriction applies only to the rep, not the schedule.
* A reportable flag/indicator captures when this scenario occurs, so these consignors/leads can be identified after the fact.
* **How this scenario is flagged and made reportable for identification purposes is documented as its own callout** — this may end up being the existing High-Value checkbox/indicator already in use, but that should be explicitly confirmed and noted rather than assumed.
* A consumable process document is created for L&D and BDRs — step-by-step with images — walking through what happens when a pre-booked appointment is later flagged High-Value (rep stays, time can change), and when a CLP-assigned rep carries into an in-home rebooking.
* Does not change standard HV escalation routing for leads that have not yet been booked — this applies only to leads with an existing pre-booked in-home appointment or existing CLP rep assignment.

fields.description:
**Summary:** Extend Title Level automation to skip updates when a title maps to null, and add mapping values for four additional titles

**Description:**  
 As a sales ops specialist, I want the Title Level automation established in Sales-9161 to skip updating a user's or sales quota record's Title Level when their title has no defined mapping, so that records aren't populated with an incorrect or blank value for titles that don't correspond to a level.

**Scope:**

* **This is a follow-on/append story to Sales-9161** — it extends that story's User Record and Sales Quota Record Title Level automation; it does not change 9161's placement, field type, or historical-locking behavior.
* If a title's mapping value is null, the Title Level field is **not updated** for that record — the automation skips it rather than writing a blank or default value.
* This null-skip behavior applies on both the User Record and the Sales Quota Record, consistent with where Sales-9161 already writes Title Level.
* Adds the following title-to-level mappings to the existing global picklist/metadata table:

| **Title** | **Title Level** |
| --- | --- |
| Resale Advisor | Level 1 |
| Elite Business Development Representative | Null |
| Sales Engagement Specialist | Null |
| Group Manager | Null |
| Group Manager, Inside Sales | Null |

* Same historical-locking rule from Sales-9161 applies — once a Sales Quota Record's Title Level is generated for a given month, it stays locked to reflect that month's title, even if the title changes later. Records skipped due to a null mapping have nothing to lock, since no value was written.
* Any historical records for June or July are backfilled for what the title levels were current for those previous months. 

‌

**Dependencies:** Depends on Sales-9161 (Title Level on User Record and Sales Quota Record) as the parent story — this cannot be built independently of that automation existing.

fields.description:
## Purpose

Time-boxed investigation into how to enable Salesforce Mocha/WebdriverIO UI automation tests to pass standard MFA (TOTP) after Salesforce enforces multi-factor authentication for all users. This spike accounts for the research conducted on 2026-07-14 that led to the creation of the implementation story \[SALES-9429\].

## Background

Salesforce is enforcing MFA for UI logins. Privileged users require phishing-resistant MFA (passkeys/WebAuthn), which is impractical for headless CI. All other users require standard MFA, where authenticator-app TOTP is acceptable. The `qe-mocha-automation` Salesforce specs currently have no MFA handling, so once enforcement is enabled, UI suites will fail at login.

## Research Questions

1. What MFA methods does Salesforce support for non-privileged users, and which are machine-solvable in a headless CI environment?
2. Can automation users be downgraded from System Administrator to a non-privileged profile (e.g., Engineers) to avoid phishing-resistant MFA while still retaining the permissions needed for test execution?
3. How does Salesforce's "Verify Your Identity" challenge screen render — what are the DOM selectors for the TOTP input field and submit button in the staging org?
4. Is `otplib` (or an equivalent Node.js TOTP library) viable for generating valid codes at runtime within the Mocha/WebdriverIO test harness?
5. What is the correct enrollment flow for third-party authenticator TOTP on Salesforce automation users, and how do we capture the Base32 secret?
6. How should TOTP secrets be securely stored and injected — what's the mapping pattern between `SF_USERn_NAME` and `SF_USERn_TOTP_SECRET` across local `.env`, 1Password, and GitHub Actions secrets?
7. Does login still work when MFA is not presented (backward compatibility during phased rollout)?
8. Are there alternative approaches (JWT Bearer / frontdoor session login) that could bypass the UI MFA challenge entirely for bots?

## Outcome

Investigation completed. Findings were documented and resulted in the implementation story \[SALES-9429|https://trr-prod.atlassian.net/browse/SALES-9429\] — "\[QE-MOCHA-AUTOMATION\] Support Salesforce standard MFA via TOTP for Mocha UI login."

## Related

* Implementation story: SALES-9429

fields.description:
Grant Revenue Ops LeanData and Sumo access to view, manage and audit routing weights and percentages, restrict GMs and sales reps.  
  
As a Revenue Ops user, I want LeanData and Sumo access to view, update, audit and report on territory pool routing weights and their resulting percentages, so that I can manage interim weighting adjustments throughout the month without depending on another team - while keeping that data out of view for GMs and sales reps to prevent over-involvement and confusion.   
  
Scope: 

* Revenue Ops is granted LeanData access neeeded to view and update routing weights and resulting distribution percentages on the territory pool’s round robin assignment.
* RevOps can audit and report on the weights and percentages -including exporting the data or linking to it for review and managment.
* RevOps can update the weights and percentages to make interim adjustments as needed during the month.
* GMS and sales reps are restricted from viewing this data and cannot view it or edit it. This is to prevent over-involvement and confusion. _(Concierge GMs and all reps today do not have access to view LeanData round robin pools and therefore cannot view the weighting of reps in a given pool. IS GMs are able to see LeanData Round Robin pools but only for pools where they’re listed as a Pool manager, which pertains to only IS Region pools and does not apply to pools with weighted reps.)_
* Documentation is provided that gives RevOps the steps to follow for adjusting the weights and percentages. 
* SRT Engineers who are managing or covering as back up for the weighting have access and visibility.
